headline: Tax-free income limit raised to Tk 400,000 for next year
summary: The government has increased the exemption threshold by Tk 25,000, though lower-income taxpayers will face a higher rate on the first taxable slab.
details: The government has raised the tax-free income threshold to Tk 400,000 for the next tax year, increasing it by Tk 25,000 from the previous limit.
Individuals earning up to Tk 400,000 between July 2025 and June 2026 will be exempt from paying income tax.
The change followed a proposal by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman during budget discussions in parliament on Monday.
The BNP government had initially proposed keeping the exemption limit unchanged from the threshold set by the interim government.
Under the revised structure, income exceeding Tk 400,000 will be taxed at 10 percent on the next Tk 300,000.
Previously, the first slab above the tax-free threshold was taxed at 5 percent, meaning lower-income taxpayers will now face a higher burden.
The amendment to the Finance Bill was approved by voice vote after being presented to Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury.
The parliamentary session was chaired by Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad, with discussions led by Leader of the House Tarique and Leader of the Opposition Shafiqur Rahman.
caption:
Good news for some, but a catch for others. Bangladesh raises the tax-free limit to Tk 400,000.

The government has raised the tax-free income threshold to Tk 400,000 for the next tax year, increasing it by Tk 25,000 from the previous limit.

Individuals earning up to Tk 400,000 between July 2025 and June 2026 will be exempt from paying income tax.

The change followed a proposal by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman during budget discussions in parliament on Monday.

The BNP government had initially proposed keeping the exemption limit unchanged from the threshold set by the interim government.

Under the revised structure, income exceeding Tk 400,000 will be taxed at 10 percent on the next Tk 300,000.

Previously, the first slab above the tax-free threshold was taxed at 5 percent, meaning lower-income taxpayers will now face a higher burden.

The amendment to the Finance Bill was approved by voice vote after being presented to Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury.

The parliamentary session was chaired by Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad, with discussions led by Leader of the House Tarique and Leader of the Opposition Shafiqur Rahman.

headline_marked: PM urges [[students to plant a tree every year]] during nationwide drive
headline: PM urges students to plant a tree every year during nationwide drive
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman launched a tree plantation program across 29,000+ secondary schools, calling students the future gamechangers.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has urged students across the country to plant at least one tree every monsoon season. He launched the nationwide tree plantation program for over 29,000 secondary educational institutions on Monday.
The program was inaugurated by planting a neem tree sapling at the open area of the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center in Agargaon, Dhaka.
During the event, the Prime Minister recalled the memory of former President Ziaur Rahman planting a neem tree in Saudi Arabia, which locals now refer to as the 'Zia Tree'.
He highlighted the benefits of tree plantation and urged teachers to encourage their students to participate actively in the green initiative.
Additionally, the Prime Minister received a Guard of Honor from the Bangladesh National Cadet Corps (BNCC) and praised their significant role in civil defense.
He announced that the government will take initiatives to expand BNCC activities at the district and upazila levels and will ensure proper investment to modernize their training programs.
caption:
One student, one tree. PM Tarique Rahman calls on the youth to lead the green revolution.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has urged students across the country to plant at least one tree every monsoon season. He launched the nationwide tree plantation program for over 29,000 secondary educational institutions on Monday.

The program was inaugurated by planting a neem tree sapling at the open area of the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center in Agargaon, Dhaka.

During the event, the Prime Minister recalled the memory of former President Ziaur Rahman planting a neem tree in Saudi Arabia, which locals now refer to as the 'Zia Tree'.

He highlighted the benefits of tree plantation and urged teachers to encourage their students to participate actively in the green initiative.

Additionally, the Prime Minister received a Guard of Honor from the Bangladesh National Cadet Corps (BNCC) and praised their significant role in civil defense.

He announced that the government will take initiatives to expand BNCC activities at the district and upazila levels and will ensure proper investment to modernize their training programs.
